attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post on Where's Your Ed At.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the firm claim about dependence on funding and his 'don't seem' hedge on the revenue part. 'They' in context means heavily valued GenAI startups like Perplexity. Generalising that to all generative AI startups is a slight stretch, but the contract discloses both readings.

contract.note: The contract discloses both the narrow and broad readings of 'they', leaves the hedged 'impressive' part unscored, and requires cash-flow evidence before calling a startup dependent on funding. That is fair to his words. Which companies 'they' covers decides the result.

evidence.note: Gamma's CEO says the company is profitable and not raising money (April 2025). This is a company statement with no cash-flow detail. It only challenges the broad reading, and Gamma is not one of the companies he discussed.
Midjourney was profitable without investors around 2022. That is outside the target quarter, with no cash-flow data. It challenges only the broad reading.
Unconfirmed reports of OpenAI's annualized revenue and projected cash burn. Neither is realized cash flow for the quarter, and neither proves OpenAI needed continuous funding.

reviews.rationale: No item gives cash-flow or liquidity data for April–June 2025 showing whether the named companies needed continuous venture funding. Gamma and Midjourney cut against the broad reading, but Gamma's evidence is a self-report and Midjourney's is from an earlier period, so neither shows cash sufficiency. Neither touches the narrow reading. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post on Where's Your Ed At.

semantics.note: He wrote 'nobody is buying' in the present tense and framed the IPO as the 'only way' with 'would be'. The draft's 'will' firms this up a little, but it broadly captures his exit-route forecast. The $3B loss figure is embedded colour, not a separate prediction.

contract.note: In context, 'access liquidity' means a whole-company exit for investors (acquisition versus IPO). Counting a partial employee tender at a higher private valuation as contradiction stretches his words against him. Partial secondary sales were already common when he wrote.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 confirms a tender in April 2026 in which existing holders sold shares. The filing itself shows the company moving to an IPO, which fits his predicted route rather than refuting it.
Bloomberg reports a partial employee tender at a $350B valuation ahead of an expected IPO. This is not an acquisition or a company-wide exit, so under a fair reading it does not contradict him.

reviews.rationale: The contract's result depends on counting a partial employee tender as 'liquidity', which is unfair to his context about exits. Under the fair reading, no acquisition at $170B or more is shown, and Anthropic has filed for an IPO. That is consistent with his forecast but does not prove the IPO was the only route. No deadline was stated, so the forecast remains open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. He cites Kedrosky but endorses the claimed chain of effects himself.

semantics.note: A firm forecast with no deadline: capex slows, then NVIDIA GPU purchases slow, then US growth slows. The draft preserves 'at some point'.

contract.note: Requiring the full chain, accepting slower growth instead of an outright decline, and not treating 'at some point' as a deadline are all fair to his words.

evidence.note: IDC: global AI infrastructure spending was flat quarter-on-quarter in Q1 2026 but up 33% year on year, and the 2026 forecast was raised. It says nothing on NVIDIA GPU purchases or US growth.

St. Louis Fed: the GDP contribution of broad investment categories fell in Q3 2025 as their growth levelled off. These categories include non-AI spending, and the analysis identifies no NVIDIA GPU channel.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The evidence shows partial slowdowns in broad investment measures, but nothing establishes the full chain from slower AI capex to fewer NVIDIA GPU purchases to lower US growth. Nothing refutes it either. No conclusive event has occurred.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post on Where's Your Ed At.

semantics.note: In context, 'they' refers to OpenAI's two figures reported in late July and on August 1, 2025. The draft says OpenAI and states it firmly, as he did ('it's clear').

contract.note: Requiring evidence on the calculations behind both figures is reasonable. It is also fair to note that a rolling window is not inherently nonstandard.

evidence.note: The CFO-sourced figure of $1B revenue for July is realized monthly revenue, a different metric. It does not reconcile the $12B and $13B annualized figures.
A June 2025 spokesperson describes the calculation as monthly revenue times 12, with stated exclusions. That is an ordinary method, but it predates the disputed reporting episode.

reviews.rationale: No disclosure gives the measurement periods, revenue coverage or calculations behind the July 30 and August 1 figures. The evidence neither shows a departure from standard annualization nor reconciles the two figures to an ordinary method.
